subtopics.title: Islamabad MoU and the 14-point roadmap
subtopics.summary: The United States and Iran signed the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding in June 2026. The MoU is an interim diplomatic framework rather than a permanent peace treaty. It provides for an immediate ceasefire, a 60-day negotiation process, and phased steps on Strait of Hormuz traffic and sanctions.

subtopics.title: Iran-U.S. nuclear diplomacy: JCPOA to 2018
subtopics.summary: The Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (2015) set limits on Iran's nuclear programme in return for easing of international sanctions. The United States withdrew from the nuclear agreement in 2018. Iran then gradually scaled back its compliance with several JCPOA commitments.

subtopics.title: Three strategic pillars and their impact
subtopics.summary: The booklet groups the accord's benefits into three pillars: regional stability, energy markets and economic development. Reopening the Strait of Hormuz is expected to cut freight and insurance costs. Persistent regional tensions and doubts about the 60-day timeline are the main challenges.
facts: Pillar 1: Strengthening regional stability, through reduced conflict risks and an improved security environment.
Pillar 2: Energy market benefits, including reduced oil price volatility.
Pillar 3: Economic developmental gains, including stimulated trade and investment.
Reopening the Strait of Hormuz reduces freight and insurance costs.
Lower crude oil prices would lower India's inflationary pressures and current account deficit.
Reintegration of Iran boosts the Chabahar Port and the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC).
Experts doubt a comprehensive settlement can be concluded within the two-month timeframe.
Tensions between Israel and Hezbollah, and Iranian regional proxies, continue to persist.

subtopics.title: IAEA: origins, objectives and leadership
subtopics.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency was founded in 1957 and is an intergovernmental organization. It grew out of the 1953 Atoms for Peace speech by US President Dwight D. Eisenhower. Its objectives are to promote peaceful use of nuclear energy and to inhibit its use for military purposes.

quizzes.passage: Nuclear diplomacy between Iran and the United States has moved through several phases. For a long period, Iran faced extensive sanctions, and its nuclear programme was the central point of dispute between the two countries. A later arrangement was reached with a group of major world powers, and it set specific terms for Iran's nuclear activities. In 2018, the United States withdrew from the nuclear agreement, and Iran then gradually scaled back its compliance with several of the commitments it had accepted. The present phase of diplomacy began in June 2026, when the United States and Iran signed the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding. The booklet describes this document as an interim diplomatic framework rather than a permanent peace treaty. The memorandum outlines a fourteen-point roadmap. It covers de-escalation of hostilities, restoration of commercial navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, discussions on sanctions relief and confidence-building measures between both countries. A proposal also envisages a comprehensive agreement backed by the UN Security Council once negotiations conclude. Phased sanctions relief and easing of restrictions on Iranian oil exports are part of the arrangement under discussion. The document also provides for oversight of implementation and for restricted assets to be unlocked. Iran has reaffirmed its nuclear pledge, and talks are to begin after key steps are taken.

quizzes.passage: Iran and the United States have been locked in a long dispute over Iran's nuclear programme. For years the country lived under extensive sanctions, which shaped its economy and its relations with the wider world. A later accord was struck between Iran and a set of major world powers. That accord placed binding limits on the programme and tied those limits to changes in the wider sanctions regime. In 2018, the United States left the agreement. Iran responded by reducing its adherence to several of the commitments it had made. The Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, signed in June 2026, is an interim diplomatic framework rather than a permanent peace treaty. Its fourteen points cover an immediate end to hostilities, restoration of commercial navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, and discussions on sanctions relief. The memorandum also includes oversight of implementation, the release of frozen funds and a proposal for a comprehensive agreement backed by the UN Security Council once negotiations conclude. Iran has reaffirmed its nuclear pledge under the document, which also includes a commitment to refrain from nuclear weapon development. Phased sanctions relief and easing of restrictions on Iranian oil exports are also part of the arrangement under discussion.

quizzes.passage: The International Atomic Energy Agency is a central body in discussions about nuclear energy and its uses. It was founded in 1957 and is headquartered in Vienna, Austria. One of its stated aims is to promote the peaceful use of nuclear energy, and this aim sits at the core of much of its work. The agency has become prominent in the current dispute between Iran and the United States. The Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, signed in June 2026, provides for downblending of highly enriched uranium under IAEA supervision. The booklet describes that memorandum as an interim diplomatic framework rather than a permanent peace treaty. The memorandum also covers restoration of commercial navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, discussions on sanctions relief, and confidence-building measures between both countries. Its fourteen points are meant to lead toward a comprehensive agreement, which the booklet says would be backed by the UN Security Council. Negotiations on nuclear issues, regional security and sanctions relief follow the initial steps. The memorandum also provides for restricted assets to be unlocked, for oversight of implementation, and for Iran to refrain from nuclear weapon development. The agency's supervision of nuclear material is part of the arrangement under discussion. Iran has also reaffirmed its nuclear pledge.

quizzes.passage: The International Atomic Energy Agency works in the field of nuclear energy and is headquartered in Vienna, Austria. It was founded in 1957. The agency's stated purpose is to promote the peaceful use of nuclear energy. It has become visible in the current dispute between Iran and the United States. The Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, signed in June 2026, provides for downblending of highly enriched uranium under IAEA supervision. The booklet describes that memorandum as an interim diplomatic framework rather than a permanent peace treaty. Its fourteen points include an immediate end to hostilities, restoration of commercial navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, and confidence-building measures between both countries. The memorandum also envisages a comprehensive agreement backed by the Security Council once negotiations conclude. Iran has reaffirmed its nuclear pledge under the document, which also includes a commitment to refrain from nuclear weapon development. The memorandum also calls for the lifting of naval restrictions and the restoration of unrestricted commercial maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Discussions on nuclear issues, regional security and sanctions relief are part of the wider process that follows these initial steps. Restricted assets are to be unlocked under the memorandum, and oversight of implementation is part of the same document.
